advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap force_issue_reindex's dc_request calls (or _request) so URLError, not just HTTPError, degrades to a no-op, matching the documented 'never raise' contract.
evidence: _dc_support.py:298-300 `status, body = dc_request(...)` then `if status != 200 ...: return` — this only handles a returned status, not an exception

tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:142 `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:` is the ONLY except clause in _request; a bare URLError (connection refused, DNS, socket timeout) is not caught and propagates
docstring at _dc_support.py:292-296 claims 'on any failure to obtain that id ... returns without reindexing and WITHOUT raising' and 'no worse off than before this helper existed'
advisory.finding: force_issue_reindex's docstring guarantees it returns WITHOUT raising 'on any failure to obtain that id' and leaves the caller 'no worse off', but the underlying dc_request (conftest._request) only catches urllib.error.HTTPError, not plain urllib.error.URLError (connection refused / DNS / timeout). A connection-level failure on the id GET (or the reindex POST) therefore propagates as an exception and aborts the pass rather than degrading to the intended no-op.
scenarios: The reindex admin resource or Jira REST endpoint drops the connection / times out at the socket level (not an HTTP status) — force_issue_reindex raises and fails the pass instead of falling back to the search wait
advisory.suggested_fix: Either broaden _request to catch urllib.error.URLError (returning a synthetic non-200), or wrap the dc_request calls inside force_issue_reindex in try/except URLError returning a sentinel status so callers still fall back to the search wait.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit case where the fake dc_request raises a URLError to confirm force_issue_reindex degrades to a no-op without propagating.
evidence: test_dc_force_reindex.py:66-71 `_RecordingRequest.__call__` always returns a queued tuple and never raises
test_dc_force_reindex.py:96 test_force_reindex_does_not_reindex_when_the_id_read_fails uses a (503, ...) tuple — an HTTP status, not an exception
ABSENCE: no test feeds a dc_request that raises urllib.error.URLError, so the documented 'WITHOUT raising' guarantee for connection-level failures is untested
advisory.finding: The unit test suite pins the no-op-on-non-200 and id-less-body paths but never exercises the path where dc_request raises (the network-error case the docstring's 'any failure' language covers), so the 'never raise' contract is asserted only for cases where the fake already cannot raise.
scenarios: A future refactor makes dc_request propagate a connection error; the unit oracle stays green while the live lane regresses

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test feeding `(200, "unexpected")` (or a list body) to force_issue_reindex asserting a single GET call, no POST, and no raise, covering the `not isinstance(body, dict)` branch.
evidence: _dc_support.py:299 `if status != 200 or not isinstance(body, dict):` — the isinstance disjunct is added behavior in this diff

test_force_reindex_does_not_reindex_when_the_id_read_fails only exercises status!=200 with body='upstream unavailable' (a str, but status is 503 so the isinstance branch is never reached): `req = _RecordingRequest([(503, "upstream unavailable")])`
ABSENCE: no test supplies a `(200, <non-dict>)` response such as `(200, "unexpected")` or `(200, ["x"])`, so the isinstance guard's no-op-without-raise contract is untested
advisory.finding: The `not isinstance(body, dict)` disjunct of the added guard (a 200 id-read whose body is a non-dict, e.g. a JSON string or list) is never exercised. The three tests cover the happy path, a non-200 read, and a dict body missing `id`, but none feeds a 200 with a non-dict body — so the isinstance half of the never-raise contract (docstring: "WITHOUT raising") is unverified. A regression dropping the isinstance check would call `.get` on a str/list and raise, and no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_force_reindex_does_not_reindex_when_the_body_is_not_a_dict` using `_RecordingRequest([(200, "unexpected")])`, asserting `len(req.calls) == 1` and that no exception is raised.
